channel.title: Agents on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Agents on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: azure: Announcing: Azure Copilot introduces direct access to agents
item.description:
Starting in August 2026, Azure Copilot will let customers interact directly with agents to move from questions to actions faster. Users can choose the agent best suited to their goal.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: How we built ThinkingBox to measure whether agents finish the job
item.description:
ThinkingBox splits the execution framework from the benchmark package so each can be updated independently. The article frames this as a way to measure whether agents actually finish tasks.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Dragon Copilot Physician Apps and Agents on Microsoft Marketplace
item.description:
Microsoft Marketplace is now a new channel for discovering, evaluating, and purchasing Dragon Copilot Physician Apps and Agents. The availability applies to Dragon Copilot customers in the United States.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: From single call to agents: five new Claude capabilities now available in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now supports five new Claude capabilities on Azure-hosted models: structured outputs, web search, web fetch, MCP connector, and tool search. The update positions a model endpoint for agent-style workflows rather than single-call usage.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 10
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s August 10 weekly release adds new models, portable plugins, and workflow improvements for agents. The updates are aimed at making Copilot more flexible across editors, the command line, and the Copilot app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Building Agents that Act on Your Behalf with Toolboxes in Foundry
item.description:
Toolboxes in Microsoft Foundry are presented as a way to let agents act on a user’s behalf while handling delegated identity across tools and services. The post highlights using a private Entra-protected MCP server alongside Microsoft’s managed Work IQ MCP server in the same agent flow.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: What’s New in Microsoft Foundry | June 2026
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry’s June 2026 update adds Claude GA and several agent-related features released between Build 2026 and the end of June. It also calls out autopilot agents, expanded Toolboxes and Routines, and Agent Optimizer entering private preview.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Toolboxes in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Toolboxes are now generally available. They provide a unified endpoint for commonly used tools in prompt agents and can also be invoked outside prompt agents.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: New features and Claude as agent provider preview in JetBrains IDEs
item.description:
GitHub added support for organization and enterprise agents in JetBrains IDEs, along with Copilot CLI message queueing/steering and a new agent debug logs summary view. The update also previews Claude as an agent provider in JetBrains IDEs.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Agentic Workflows is now in public preview
item.description:
GitHub Agentic Workflows is now in public preview. It lets you automate reasoning-based tasks such as issue triage, CI failure analysis, and documentation updates using coding agents inside GitHub.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Discovery to Execution: Scaling Agents with Toolboxes and Routines in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry is adding new Toolbox capabilities, including Skills, to help teams discover, manage, and secure tools for production agent workflows. The update is aimed at scaling agents from small-scale use to production execution.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: commandline: Turn specs into evals for any agent with ASSERT
item.description:
ASSERT is an open-source framework that turns natural-language behavior requirements into executable evaluations for AI models and agents. It is designed for evaluation and regression testing from written specs.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: Microsoft Build 2026: Securing code, agents, and models across the development lifecycle
item.description:
Microsoft says Build 2026 introduced MDASH and additional security capabilities aimed at securing code, agents, and models across the development lifecycle. The post frames these updates as support for fast AI development with security controls built in.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: ai: Build and run agents at scale with Microsoft Foundry at Build 2026
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry is presented as a platform for building, deploying, and operating production-ready agents. The post highlights Agent Framework, Toolboxes, hosted agents, Microsoft 365 distribution, observability, and agent optimization.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Foundry IQ: Build smarter agents faster with unified knowledge and serverless retrieval
item.description:
Foundry IQ is presented as a way to ground agents in unified enterprise knowledge using serverless retrieval. The post emphasizes improved agentic retrieval quality and production-ready security.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: What’s new in Microsoft Foundry | Build Edition
item.description:
Microsoft Build 2026 introduces several Microsoft Foundry updates for agent developers, including hosted runtimes, Toolboxes, memory, Voice Live, Foundry IQ, new models, managed compute, and added trust, evaluation, and observability features.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: devops+ai: 🔥Designing Specialized Agents - Model Selection, Tool Scoping, and Output Contracts🔥
item.description:
The article frames specialized agents as being given a limited toolbox and clear instructions. It points to three design areas: choosing the model, scoping the tools it can use, and defining output contracts.

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: commandline: Disposable agents, durable memory: The architecture behind Squad
item.description:
The article describes Squad, a file-backed agent-team architecture built around human oversight. It emphasizes inspectable memory, explicit orchestration, and moving governance rules from prompts into code.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: Inside the Microsoft Agent Framework: How we designed a layered SDK
item.description:
Microsoft describes the Agent Framework as a layered SDK that supports different agent architectures. It highlights agent loops, workflows, and harnesses as the main building blocks for both simple assistants and more complex multi-agent systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog
